articles.summary: At several oncology conferences this year, one theme emerged consistently: biomarkers have evolved from valuable scientific tools into indispensable strategic assets in oncology development. As oncology science advances, therapeutic approaches are becoming increasingly complex. Cell and gene therapies, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), and immunotherapies all require a deeper understanding of disease biology and patient response.

articles.summary: The neurology landscape has become increasingly dynamic over the past decade. As amyloid targeting therapies for Alzheimer's disease (AD) and other neurodegenerative disorders advance, the industry's focus has shifted away from PET imaging to cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and more recently, blood-based biomarkers of amyloid and Tau pathology. For drug developers, biomarkers are no longer supplementary research tools. They are becoming essential components of clinical development strategies, patient selection and therapeutic decision-making.
articles.title: Neurology Drug Development in 2026: Biomarker Trends Reshaping Clinical Trials
